Job Description
Mine Warfare Managers supervise maintenance on service mine systems, exercise and training mine systems, and underwater targets; perform exercise
and training and service mine upgrades/downgrades; supervise ordnance handling and mine equipment usage; monitor issue/turn-ins of logistics material;
control maintenance of magazines, ready service lockers, and inert storage areas; support tactical operations utilizing sophisticated computer, sensor, and
communications systems; conduct precision navigation; operate and maintain Mine Countermeasures (MCM) systems, including unmanned systems, to
locate and neutralize sea mines; employ physical oceanography and bathymetric measuring devices; employ internal and external communication devices
and circuits; review various log keeping and administrative functions associated with combat systems employment; manage the assembly, disassembly,
rigging, and unrigging of deck equipment in support of MCM, Underway Replenishment (UNREP), towing, salvage, Search and Rescue (SAR), and ship
and small boat navigation operations; teach basic marlinspike seamanship; supervise operations and maintenance of deck equipment; oversee shipboard
preservation; Plan, Brief, Execute, Debrief (PBED) tactical operations; ensure safe passage of national and global assets; and perform sector defense.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
